text:
Connor Brown has been one of the quiet contributors to a Devils team that has won eight of ten: 10 points in 13 games, five of them goals, and five points in his last two outings against Washington. His minutes have crept up lately, nearly 20 on Nov. 14.

We'd be careful with the goals. He's shooting 29.4% on 17 shots, roughly double what our talent range expects, and his scoring rate of 3.0 points per 60 is well above the 1.8 to 2.5 we'd consider his real level. Thirteen games is a small sample, and it shows.

The bigger worry is five on five. New Jersey gets just 46% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 12 points worse than without him. He's a 32-year-old sixth-round pick who has made a long career out of being useful, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with a real skill: 19% of his setups cross the royal road, nearly triple a typical forward. Enjoy the points. Watch the chances.
